name: A CAPITAL HONOR
clue: Founded for freed Black Americans, this West African nation named its capital for the U.S. president in office at the time

name: SILVERWARE
clue: Donated in 1892 by Canada's governor general, this trophy carries the engraved names of its champions

name: THE SCOTTISH POWER PLAY
clue: The Scot whose improved steam engines drove the Industrial Revolution lends his name to this unit, one joule per second

name: PAINLESS OPERATION
clue: The director's 14-year-old son wrote the lyrics to 'Suicide Is Painless,' the theme of this war comedy

name: ONE STEP AHEAD
clue: Move each letter of this film's murderous computer's name one step along the alphabet and you get IBM

name: GUAC OF FAME
clue: Its name comes from the Nahuatl 'ahuacatl,' and its Hass variety traces back to one tree grown by a California mailman

name: NAMED FOR DAD
clue: Charles II named this colony not for its Quaker founder but for his late father, an admiral the king owed money

name: WHAT'S IN A NO-NAME?
clue: Odysseus gave this fake name, so when the blinded Polyphemus howled for help, the other Cyclopes thought nothing was wrong

name: THE GIFT THAT NEVER GROWS UP
clue: In 1929 J.M. Barrie gave the rights to this play to London's Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children

name: WHEELS IN THE SKY
clue: The six-star emblem of this Japanese carmaker shows the Pleiades cluster, which is what its name means

name: TAKE A HINT
clue: In this composer's 'Farewell' Symphony, players snuff their candles and walk out one by one, a hint to their prince

name: PUCCINI'S HEIRS
clue: An update of Puccini's 'La Bohème,' this 1996 musical lost its creator hours before its first off-Broadway preview

name: X MARKS THE START
clue: A map Robert Louis Stevenson drew to amuse his stepson on a rainy Scottish holiday grew into this 1883 novel

name: LANDLORD LESSONS
clue: Lizzie Magie's 'The Landlord's Game,' meant to expose the evils of hoarding land, evolved into this classic

name: LOOKING UP TO IT
clue: Opened in 1889, this structure stood as the world's tallest until New York's Chrysler Building passed it in 1930

name: CHANGE OF NUMBERS
clue: To avoid clashing with Leon Uris' 'Mila 18,' Joseph Heller's 1961 novel swapped the 18 in its title for this

name: NAME CHANGE
clue: Founded in 1703, this city was Russia's capital for two centuries and went by two other names before reclaiming its first

name: HEAVENLY METAL
clue: Named for a planet found just eight years before it, this element identified in 1789 later fueled the bomb dropped on Hiroshima

name: WRONG WAY ROUND
clue: Odd but true: a ship sailing this famous waterway from the Atlantic to the Pacific ends up farther east than where it began

name: TORTOISE TERRITORY
clue: Named for an old Spanish word for their giant tortoises, this Ecuadorian archipelago gave Darwin food for thought
